sections.h2: Where is the Hardin County Clerk's office, and what does it record for a home seller?
sections.html:
The Hardin County Clerk's office is in the county government building at 150 N. Provident Way, Suite 103, Elizabethtown, KY 42701. It is open Monday through Friday from 7:45 am to 4:30 pm, and the main number is 270-765-2171. A second branch at 101 W. Lincoln Trail Blvd in Radcliff handles vehicle registration on Tuesday through Thursday.

The clerk keeps the deed and mortgage records for the county, along with marriage licenses, assumed names, voter registration and motor vehicle titles. For a seller, the office matters at three points: when you record the deed to the buyer, when you need a release of an old mortgage on file, and when a past due tax bill has moved to the clerk and needs a payoff.

The county government's own page also lists a delinquent tax calculator and tax sale information, both handled through the clerk.

sections.h2: Where must a Kentucky deed be recorded?
sections.html:
A deed goes to the county clerk in the county where the property, or most of it, is located, under KRS 382.110. For a house in Elizabethtown, Radcliff, Vine Grove or anywhere else in Hardin County, that means this office. A parcel that crosses the line into Meade, Bullitt or LaRue County is recorded where the greater part sits.

The same statute tells the clerk not to accept a deed that fails to name the source of the grantor's title. Where the grantor got the property by recorded deed, the new deed cites the earlier one by book, page and recording date. If the grantor inherited it, the deed explains how and from whom. Mortgage holders who take a deed in lieu of foreclosure have 45 days from signing to file it.

sections.h2: What must a Hardin County deed contain before the clerk accepts it?
sections.html:
Kentucky adds several content rules in KRS 382.135, and the clerk may not accept a deed that misses them. A deed prepared by a title attorney will include each item, but a form downloaded for a family transfer often does not.

  • The full names and mailing addresses of the grantor and grantee.
  • A statement of the full consideration.
  • An in care of address where the property tax bill for the transfer year may be sent.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate from both sides that the stated consideration is the full price, or for a gift, a certificate stating that it is a gift and giving the estimated fair cash value.

When property passes by will or intestacy, the personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk of each county holding land. It lists who received each parcel and the value used in handling the estate.

sections.h2: How much does the Hardin County Clerk charge to record documents?
sections.html:
The clerk publishes a fee schedule with filing standards. Paper documents should be white, 8.5 by 11 inches preferred, with a 3 inch blank margin at the top of the first page and one inch elsewhere, black ink, and no staples or seals. Electronic recording runs through Simplifile, ePn or CSC.

Selected Hardin County Clerk recording fees, from the clerk's fee schedule
DocumentFee
Deed, easement or deed of restrictions$50.00
Affidavit of descent and distribution$50.00
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46.00
Affidavit$46.00
Mortgage$80.00
Power of attorney$50.00
Will$47.00
Certified copy$5.00

Deeds and most other documents add $3.00 for each page over five, and $4.00 for each additional reference. A mortgage adds $3.00 per page past 30 pages. Ask the clerk to confirm the total before you mail a package, since the amounts are updated on the schedule.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does a seller pay in Hardin County?
sections.html:
Kentucky's real estate transfer tax is fifty cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, and it falls on the grantor named in the deed. The county clerk calculates it and collects it before the deed is recorded, under KRS 142.050. The clerk keeps 5 percent for the collection work and sends the rest to the county treasurer every three months.

For a sale, value means the full price including any lien amounts. For a gift or a deed with nominal consideration it means the estimated open market price. As a worked example, a Hardin County house at the Census median owner occupied value of $225,800 divides into 452 blocks of $500, so the tax comes to $226.

Several transfers are exempt, including those under a foreclosure or deed in lieu, between spouses or former spouses in a divorce, between parent and child with only nominal consideration, on partition, and from a trustee to a successor trustee. A deed that only confirms or corrects an earlier one also qualifies.

sections.h2: How does the clerk fit into delinquent property tax in Hardin County?
sections.html:
The sheriff collects current year bills and sends anything unpaid to the clerk after April 15. The sheriff's office tells sellers to call the clerk at 270-765-2171 for the payoff amount on any delinquent prior year bill, since the sheriff no longer holds it.

A title company will want that figure before a closing, and it changes month by month as interest accrues. A certificate that has been sold to a third party buyer is paid to that buyer instead. Asking for the payoff in writing, dated close to the closing date, avoids a surprise at the table.

The clerk's office also records the lien, the lien release and the delinquency assignment documents, which appear in the fee schedule at $30.00 for a certificate assignment and $46.00 for a reassignment or release.

sections.h2: What local numbers frame a Hardin County sale?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 44,622 households in the county with 2.44 people per household, and 84.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. The 2025 estimate for housing units is 51,149, and median gross rent is $971. Per capita income is $37,638 and 12,344 residents are veterans.

With Fort Knox in the county, a share of sellers and buyers are on a tight moving timeline, so a deed that meets every content rule the first time saves a trip back to Suite 103. An absent in care of address or a missing notarized consideration certificate keeps a deed from being accepted.

  • Check the deed against the content list above before you leave the title office.
  • Pay the transfer tax and recording fee together at filing.
  • Ask for a certified copy ($5.00) if the lender or title company wants proof of recording.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a house in Hardin County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: At the Hardin County Clerk's office, 150 N. Provident Way, Suite 103, Elizabethtown. State law requires recording in the county where the property sits. Electronic recording is accepted through Simplifile, ePn and CSC.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Hardin County?
faqs.a: The clerk's schedule lists $50.00 for a deed, plus $3.00 for each page over five. The grantor also pays transfer tax of $0.50 per $500 of value, collected at filing.

faqs.q: Can I skip the transfer tax by gifting my house to a relative?
faqs.a: Only in the narrow case the statute covers. A transfer between parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, with only nominal consideration is exempt. A gift to anyone else is taxed on the estimated market value.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed is missing the in care of address?
faqs.a: The clerk cannot accept it for record. KRS 382.135 requires an in care of address for the tax bill, along with names, mailing addresses and the notarized consideration certificate.

faqs.q: Who do I call for the payoff on an unpaid Hardin County tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Hardin County Clerk at 270-765-2171 for any prior year bill that moved from the sheriff. Current year bills are paid to the sheriff's tax department at 270-765-5133, option 1.
